item: every graceful stop stops the background jobs before the first disposal, and a job past the deadline can no longer write after it (R689)
key_paths: src/safety/shutdown.py; src/safety/uninstall.py; src/database/after_shutdown.py; src/database/writer.py; src/database/session.py; src/jobs/background.py; src/api/main.py; tests/test_shutdown_refuses_straggler_jobs.py
summary: BEFORE: the in-app power button (and the update, memory-guard and data-volume stops, all through request_shutdown) and the uninstall's stop disposed the engine BEFORE signalling, so on the stop path people actually use the pool was closed while the collector and the background jobs were still writing; they reopened it, the lifespan's stop-all came after, and its own disposal read EARLIER_DISPOSAL. And a job the 5 s stop-all gave up on (the LLM bulk queue checks its flag only after a whole generation, the Insights backlog between 300-article batches) kept writing after the disposal, because Engine.dispose() only empties the pool and the next checkout opens a fresh connection. NOW: the stop threads no longer dispose; the signal runs the lifespan's one order (scheduler stop, stop-all, write-back, disposal). After the stop-all deadline the lifespan names the threads of the jobs still running to src.database.after_shutdown, and from then on every statement, commit and write-gate acquire on those threads raises WriteAfterShutdownRefused, logged once per job by its kind; every other thread is untouched and the next start forgets them. WAITS for the jobs: power button, update, memstop, data-volume guard, uninstall, Ctrl-C/SIGTERM. Does NOT wait, deliberately: the panic wipe. Stated limit: a raw-connection write already past the write gate at the deadline can still commit. Release line: Stopping the app from its power button now lets background jobs finish their current step before the database closes, and a job that is still running then can no longer write to it after the close.
